scores.evidence: Depends on: V0 passes; T1 (tenancy model) locked; T2 (idempotency) locked
scores.rationale: Mostly substrate-upward with gates, but flaws: Phase 0 depends on T1/T2 while T1 is validated only in Phase 1, and V-numbering is inconsistent (V2/V3 differ between tables).

scores.evidence: Git commit → GitHub Actions pipeline → ... → deploy to ECS (dev environment) → run smoke test.
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real end-to-end slice through API, DB, replication, deploy and rollback, though internal-only rather than prod.

scores.evidence: T1: Tenancy model | R3 | Shared schema, row-level security | ... | Flip condition: If compliance audit or tenant size demands isolation... flip to schema-per-tenant
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions are tabulated with reversibility, default, validation and flip conditions, plus labeled assumptions.

scores.evidence: T1 (tenancy model) affects every query and schema; T3 (consistency) affects every write path; both locked before Phase 1 hardening.
scores.rationale: Widest decisions come first, but within-phase task ordering is not explicitly by blast radius (e.g., endpoints listed before auth hardening in Phase 1).

scores.evidence: Phase 0: Auth stubbed (accept any tenant_id); no real card data | Phase 1: JWT tenant_id validation; SQL injection tests; isolation gate
scores.rationale: Security has concrete content in every phase, including Phase 0 gateway auth and no-sensitive-logs.

scores.evidence: CloudWatch metrics: invoice create latency (p50, p95, p99), ledger write latency, replication lag; Alert if replication lag >10s
scores.rationale: Observability is concrete in Phase 0 and extended in each subsequent phase.

scores.evidence: DB schema in version control; Docker image pinned by hash; manual rollback procedure
scores.rationale: Reproducibility is present each phase but thin and uneven (Phase 3 is just tests; no IaC or data seeding specifics).

scores.evidence: Injected failure (kill primary DB, trigger failover) → request fails gracefully (500 error logged, alert fires); no data corruption.
scores.rationale: Failure handling appears in Phase 0 and each later phase: circuit breaker, DLQ, backup/DR, canary rollback, retries.

scores.evidence: N/A — no AI component. System is deterministic financial processing; no LLM, fine-tuning, RAG, or agentic decision-making needed.
scores.rationale: Plan explicitly declares the AI layer N/A and adds no AI components.

scores.evidence: Multi-currency support — pulled forward if tenant contract specifies EUR or GBP revenue
scores.rationale: Deferred items are listed with explicit pull-forward conditions and blockers.

note: Strong plan with a real skeleton, tradeoff table, and deferral list; weaker on gate numbering consistency, within-phase blast-radius ordering, and reproducibility depth.
